newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS SET FOR 'UNITED NATIONS' LINE-UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS SET FOR 'UNITED NATIONS' LINE-UP.

text.p: Scottish soccer champions Rangers could be left without a single native player in their first team line-up next season, following signings of two more foreign players.

The Glasgow club paid out eight million pounds ($13.1 million) on Thursday for Fiorentina central defender Lorenzo Amoruso and full-back Staale Stensaas of Rosenborg to bring the number of non-Scots reporting for pre-season training at Ibrox next month to 14.
And the buying may not end with Italian Amoruso and Norwegian Stensaas.

German goalkeeper Georg Koch is due to fly into Scotland next week to complete his move from Fortuna Dusseldorf while manager Walter Smith will learn within the next 48 hours if his 3.5 million pounds sterling bid for Inter Milan's Massimo Paganin has been successful.
The foreign legion means a bleak picture for the home-based players at Ibrox, all of whom may earn little more than fringe places in the forthcoming season.
Smith is committed to trying to establish Rangers -- one of the wealthiest clubs in Europe -- as a serious challenger in the European Cup Champions' League.
Already he has added Australian full-back Tony Vidmar, Swedish midfielder Jonas Thern, Italian teenager Rino Gattuso and now Amoruso and Stensaas to his squad, with Koch and Paganin pending.
He is also looking for a top-class striker, with Boligna's Swedish goalscorer Kennet Anderson a favourite.
Amoruso revealed he had turned down a bigger offer from Manchester United -- which would have meant 1.55 million pounds more to Fiorentina -- to join Rangers.
"I wanted to keep my promise to the Rangers chairman David Murray, because he is a good person. Sure, Manchester United is a good club, but so is Rangers," Amoruso said.
Amoruso, signed from Bari two years ago, has played 89 games in serie A and scored eight goals. His last game in Italy will be against Sampdoria on Sunday.
Manager Smith admitted his dressing room will be like the United Nations, but stated: "I don't see any other way forward for clubs like us from smaller countries."

A Rangers line-up next season could comprise: Koch (Germany), Vidmar (Australia), Stensaas (Norway), Petric (Yugoslavia), Bjorklund (Sweden), Amoruso (Italy), Laudrup (Denmark), Thern (Sweden), Rozental (Chile), Albertz (Germany) and Van Vossen (Holland). On the bench: Gascoigne (England), Moore (Australia), Bo Andersen (Denmark), Gattuso (Italy).
